flags.name: name
flags.description: Return properties whose `name` slug matches, compared case-insensitively. `?name=story-points` matches the property whose `display_name` is `Story Points`.

flags.name: display-name
flags.description: Return properties whose `display_name` matches, compared case-insensitively. `?display_name=severity` matches `Severity`.

flags.name: external-id
flags.description: Return properties whose `external_id` matches exactly. Use it to find the property you created earlier for a field in another system.

flags.name: external-source
flags.description: Return properties from one source system, for example `jira`. Combine it with `external_id`, because an `external_id` is unique only within its source.

flags.name: order-by
flags.description:
Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending.

- `sort_order` , `-sort_order`: the configured display order of the fields
- `created_at` , `-created_at`: when each property was defined
- `id` , `-id`

Order by `sort_order` when you show the fields to a person. It is the order the project itself uses.

flags.name: per-page
flags.description: Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most projects define far fewer than 50 properties, so one page is usually the whole catalog.

flags.name: offset
flags.description: Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Use the `next` value from the response instead of computing offsets yourself.

flags.name: paginate
flags.description: Set to `cursor` to switch to the keyset envelope, which skips the `COUNT` query and returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Leave it out to get the default offset envelope.

flags.name: count
flags.description: Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT(*)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response.

flags.name: fields
flags.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Fields you don't request are left out of the response instead of coming back as `null`, so a missing key means you didn't ask for it and `null` means the value is null. `id` is always included, whether or not you name it.

Pass `all` to get every requestable field. An unknown field name returns `400` with the list of valid names and the closest match, so a typo is caught instead of being silently ignored.

Requestable here: `created_at`, `default_value`, `description`, `display_name`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `logo_props`, `name`, `options`, `property_type`, `relation_type`, `settings`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`, `validation_rules`.

See [Sparse fields](/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields).

flags.name: cursor
flags.description: Opaque next_cursor continuation documented by the list response.
